title: First-Principles DFT Study of Ferroelectric-to-Antiferroelectric Phase Transitions in LiTaO$_3$ under Electric Boundary Conditions
abstract: Ferroelectric and antiferroelectric phases of LiTaO$_3$ compete under different electric boundary conditions. First-principles density-functional calculations show that the high-symmetry reference structure supports two relevant unstable $Γ$ modes: a polar $A_{2u}$ mode at $181i$ cm$^{-1}$ that condenses into the ferroelectric (FE) phase, and an antipolar $A_{2g}$ mode at $103i$ cm$^{-1}$ that condenses into the antiferroelectric (AFE) phase. Under short-circuit conditions the FE phase is the global minimum, with a well depth of $\approx 144$ meV. Under open-circuit conditions the FE phase is destabilized by the unscreened depolarization field and the AFE phase becomes the ground state, with a well depth of $\approx 19$ meV. A weakly unstable longitudinal-optic mode at $48.3i$ cm$^{-1}$ yields a well of only $\approx 0.24$ meV and is thermodynamically irrelevant. Mapping the free energy versus electric displacement $D$ locates a second-order FE$\leftrightarrow$AFE transition at $D_c=0.051$ C/m$^2$, lower than the corresponding $0.07$ C/m$^2$ in LiNbO$_3$ and therefore more accessible experimentally.
summary: This theoretical study uses DFT to map the phase competition between ferroelectric and antiferroelectric states in LiTaO3. By analyzing the free energy under varying electric boundary conditions, the authors pinpoint a second-order phase transition at a specific critical electric displacement. This work is significant because it predicts an experimentally accessible pathway for switching between these two technologically relevant phases.
main_problem: The study investigates how competing ferroelectric (FE) and antiferroelectric (AFE) phases in LiTaO3 are selected by external electric boundary conditions.
main_result: The system undergoes a second-order FE-AFE phase transition at a critical electric displacement D_c = 0.051 C/m^2, which is more accessible experimentally than in similar materials.
method: The research employs first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations combined with phonon analysis and free-energy mapping techniques.
model_or_system: The physical system is Lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), a ferroelectric perovskite oxide. The analysis models the competition between the FE and AFE states by calculating the free energy ($\Phi$) as a function of the electric displacement field (D).
key_observables: Free energy minima depths for FE and AFE phases, the critical electric displacement D_c, and the soft mode frequencies (A_2u and A_2g).
important_parameters: Boundary conditions (Short-Circuit vs. Open-Circuit), electric displacement D, and the comparison to LiNbO3 parameters.
main_assumptions: The calculations utilize DFT with the local density approximation (LDA) and incorporate the depolarization energy term to account for boundary effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the atomic structure and eigenvectors of the soft modes, and show the free energy ($\Phi$) landscapes for FE and AFE phases under different boundary conditions and as a function of D.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the stability of the FE and AFE phases under both short-circuit and open-circuit boundary conditions, mapping the free energy landscape versus electric displacement D to locate the second-order transition point.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter ferroelectrics, the methodology of mapping phase stability via free energy minimization under external fields (D) is a general technique applicable to understanding phase transitions in complex quantum or many-body systems.
